[{"id": "nnvMTG5Sl5", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "🫂Ministries Manual", "col": 12}}, {"id": "B-CtTCmVDX", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The ministries module contains features related to functions and specific ministries of the church.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "w8oEjl0tNc", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "🗓️Functions", "col": 12}}, {"id": "riOh9J0you", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Church functions are used to track attendance and for linking to other documents.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "6k3AeERCdQ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When creating a function, note the following:
- Default function types are provided, but additional function types can be created.
    - When creating a function type, you can choose an existing function as a 'template function'. This will allow you to click the 'Fill From Template' button when creating this type of function in the future to fill in most of the function details using the template function's values. Set the function's Start Date first: the schedule moves to that date and keeps its times.
- Other documents can be linked as items in the function's schedule (i.e. Songs, Sermons, People, Bible References, etc)
- Attendance can be tracked (Additional attendance types can be added if needed)
    - To pre-populate attendance for a function, you can select a 'template function' in the related function type. Then clicking the 'Fill From Template' button will pre-populate all attendance records from the template function.
- To publish a function to the public website, check the 'Publish' checkbox.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "_0iXv3IWcn", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Ministries workspace includes links to function and attendance reports.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "TvoZni0RtF", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Hint: in the Function list view, change the view type to 'Calendar' to view the Functions on a calendar.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "att-portal-h3", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "📋Attendance in the Portal", "col": 12}}, {"id": "att-portal-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Members can see their own attendance on the Attendance page of the portal. It lists every function that has them in its attendance, newest first, with their attendance type (for example Checked-In or Signed-Up).
- Functions dated after today are not shown. A recurring function copies its attendance roster onto the next occurrence before it happens, so those rows are not yet a record of who came.
- To let members correct their own attendance, tick Members Can Change Their Attendance in Portal Settings. Each row then offers Confirmed (I was there) and Absent (I was not there), and the function's attendance total updates to match. A Checked-In row can only be changed in the desk, on the Function.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "recur-h2-001", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "🔁Recurring Functions", "col": 12}}, {"id": "recur-desc-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A function can recreate itself automatically on a schedule (e.g. a weekly Bible Study). Once an occurrence's end date/time passes, the next one is created with the same schedule, attendance roster, associations, and other template details.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "recur-desc-02", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "To enable recurrence on a Function:
- Expand the Recurrence section and check Automatically Recreate.
- Choose a Repeat Frequency (Daily, Weekly, Monthly, or Yearly), and (where applicable) the day of week or day of month.
- Optionally set a Repeat Until date to stop creating new occurrences after that date.
- Uncheck Automatically Recreate at any time to stop generating new occurrences.
Tip: open a Ministry and click Create Recurring Function to start a new recurring function pre-linked to that ministry. Each ministry's Recurring Functions list shows all of the recurring functions associated with the ministry.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fsu-h2-001", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "📝Function Sign-Ups", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fsu-desc-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Function sign-ups allow people to indicate their intent to attend a function and optionally bring/complete specific items.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fsu-desc-02", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When creating a sign-up, note the following:
- Only Functions that have Allow Sign-Ups enabled will be available in the 'Function' field.
- Each person can only have one sign-up per function.
- The Attending checkbox indicates whether the person plans to attend.
    - Checking this will automatically add an attendance record to the Function with a status of: 'Signed-Up'
    - Unchecking this will remove any attendance record for the Person from the Function
- If the Function has sign-up items defined, you can add rows to indicate which (and how many of those) items you will bring/complete.
    - The Signed Up quantity on each item in the Function document will automatically update to reflect the total quantity indicated in sign-ups.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fsu-h3-001", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "📦Sign-Up Items", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fsu-item-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Sign-up items represent things that are needed for a function (e.g. food, supplies, jobs, etc). They are added to a function's Sign-Up Items table with the quantity needed. As people submit sign-ups and indicate they will bring specific items, the Quantity Signed Up on the function is automatically totaled across all sign-ups and displayed on the Function document.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "team-h2-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "🙋Ministry Teams", "col": 12}}, {"id": "team-desc-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A ministry team is the people who serve in a ministry, such as greeters, ushers or nursery workers. Churchit asks each person by email if they can serve at a function, and keeps their answer.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "team-h3-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "🧩Positions", "col": 12}}, {"id": "team-pos-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A Ministry Team Position is one job on a ministry's team (e.g. Greeter in the Hospitality ministry).
- Add the people who can fill the position under People. Only these people can be assigned to it.
- Check Needs Background Check when the position needs a current, cleared Background Check (e.g. Nursery Worker).
- Under Required Checks, pick the checks the position needs, for example Criminal Background and Child Safety Training. Each one must be cleared and still current on the day of the function. Leave it blank to accept any cleared check.
- Tick Block People Without Checks to refuse an assignment for someone without the checks. Without it, you only get a warning.
- When you add someone to the position's People who does not have the checks, you get a warning, but they stay on the list.
- On the Ministry, set the Team Coordinator, who gets an email when someone declines, and Remind Days Before: how many days before a function the people serving get a reminder. 0 sends no reminders. The ministry's positions show under Connections.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "team-h3-02", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "📋Team Needs and Assignments", "col": 12}}, {"id": "team-need-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "On a Function, list the positions it needs, and how many people each needs, in the Ministry Team section. Recurring functions and Fill from Template copy these needs from the template.
To ask a person to serve, make a Ministry Team Assignment from the Connections of the function: choose the position and the person. A warning shows when:
- a Ministry Team Block covers the date of the function
- the person already serves at another function at the same time
- the position needs a background check and the person has no current, cleared one
- the person has no email address
A warning does not stop the save. The function, position and person cannot change after the save: delete the assignment and make a new one.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "team-h3-03", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "✉️Emails and Answers", "col": 12}}, {"id": "team-email-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Once a day, each person gets one email that lists their new assignments. To send the waiting emails at once, click Send Emails Now on the Ministry Team Assignment list. Each assignment has a link to accept or decline it, with an optional reason. The link works without signing in. Members can also answer on the Ministry Team page of the portal, where they see the Schedule of each function they serve at. A person can change their answer until the function starts.
- The Status of the assignment shows the answer: Pending, Accepted or Declined.
- When someone declines, the Team Coordinator of the ministry gets an email, and the place is open again in the schedule.
- A reminder goes out the ministry's Remind Days Before ahead of the function, to each person who has not declined.
- No email goes out until the site has an outgoing Email Account. Change the words of the three emails in Email Templates: Ministry Team Request, Ministry Team Reminder and Ministry Team Decline.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "team-email-02", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "To write to everyone serving at a function, click Ministry Team → Email the Team on the Function. The email goes to each person asked to serve who has not declined. They are in BCC, so no one sees the others' email addresses. The email is kept on the function's timeline, and a message names anyone without an email address.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "team-h3-cal", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "📅Calendar", "col": 12}}, {"id": "team-cal-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Members can see the functions they accepted in the calendar on their phone or computer. On the Ministry Team page of the portal, they click Make a calendar link, then Subscribe, or copy the link into their calendar app (in Google Calendar: Other calendars, From URL). The calendar keeps itself up to date.
Anyone with the link can see where the member serves. Stop this link and make a new one replaces a link that was shared by mistake.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "team-h3-04", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "🚫Blocked Dates", "col": 12}}, {"id": "team-block-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A Ministry Team Block holds the dates a person cannot serve, such as a vacation. Check Whole Household to block everyone in their family. Members add and remove their own blocks on the Ministry Team page of the portal. On a site with branch churches, only the person's own church can add a Ministry Team Block for them. Staff at another church ask that church, or the person adds the block on the Ministry Team page.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "team-h3-05", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "🗓️Ministry Team Schedule", "col": 12}}, {"id": "team-report-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Ministry Team Schedule report shows the positions of each function in a date range: how many people each needs, how many accepted or did not answer yet, how many places are open, and who was asked. Check Only Open Positions to see the gaps. On a Function, Ministry Team → Schedule opens the report for that function.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "team-served-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Each person's Last Served and Times Served (90 Days), on the Connections tab of the Person form, count the functions where they accepted an assignment. Pending and declined requests do not count. Filter the Person list on them to find, for example, people who have not served lately.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fci-h2-001", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "✅Function Check-Ins", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fci-desc-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Function check-ins are a record that a person has physically arrived at a function.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fci-desc-02", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When creating a check-in, note the following:
- Each person can only be checked in once per function.
- Upon saving, the person's attendance record on the function will automatically be set to Checked-In.
- Deleting a check-in will remove the associated Checked-In attendance record from the function.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fci-h3-station", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "🖥️Check-In Station", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fci-station-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Check-In Station is the quickest way to check people in as they arrive:
1. Choose the Function at the top of the page. The station remembers the last function used on that computer and otherwise picks the next function on the calendar. The arrow in the field (or the function name above the Checked In list) opens the Function itself.
2. Type part of a name, a nickname, a family name, or a phone number. Results are grouped by family so parents and children can be checked in together. People who have a 'Death' life event are not listed.
3. Tap the people who have arrived (or Select all for a family) and click Check In. Pressing Enter checks in a single match straight away.
4. First-time visitors: click New Visitor (or the Add them as a new visitor link when a search finds no one), confirm the name and phone taken from what you typed, and they are created and checked in at once. Their 'Source' is Check-In and their 'Membership' is Visitor, so the member directory does not list them.
The Checked In list on the right shows everyone at the function with a button to reprint a name tag or undo a check-in. Untick Print name tags to check people in without printing.
The station is also reachable from the Check-In Station button on any Function.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fci-scan-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Scan Card. A person can show their Member QR Card instead of saying their name. Click Scan Card next to the search box and hold the card in front of the camera. The station shows the person and their family, as a name search does. Tap the people who arrived and click Check In, or press Enter to check in only the card holder. If the station cannot find the person, it shows \"No one found for this card\". The camera works only on a site that uses https. The station finds the same people as a name search. If your church keeps people private, a card from another church finds no one, except at a Function that is shared with all churches.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fci-h3-pickup", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "🧒Verify Pickup", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fci-pickup-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Use Verify Pickup when an adult comes to collect a child. It works only when Print Security Codes is ticked in Check-In Settings, because the code comes from the pickup tag.
1. Click Verify Pickup at the top of the Check-In Station.
2. Type the 4 characters of the security code on the adult's pickup tag. Press Enter or click Verify.
3. The station shows each person who was checked in with this code today, with their photo and the Function. Below them, it shows who may collect them: the Adults of the household and the family's Authorized Pickups, with their photos, relationship and notes.
4. Compare the adult at the desk with these people. Release the child only to one of them.
5. Keep a tick beside each child the adult is taking, and click Release beside the adult. Churchit records on each child's Function Check-In who collected them, when, and which volunteer released them. The station then shows \"Collected by\" with the time, and the child cannot be released again.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fci-pickup-02", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "If the station shows No child is checked in with this code today, do not release the child. Ask a member of staff. A code from an earlier day does not work. If the station shows two families, ask for the child's name.
To see who collected the children of a function, open the Function Check-In list and add the Collected By and Collected At columns. Only people the station shows can be released; for anyone else, ask a member of staff.
With more than one church, the station finds only the check-ins of Functions in your church and of Functions that are shared with all churches.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fci-h3-tags", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "🏷️Name Tags", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fci-tags-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A name tag prints for every check-in made at the station. Name tags can also be printed from a Function Check-In (Print Name Tag), for several check-ins from the Function Check-In list (Actions → Print Name Tags), or for any people without a check-in from the Person list (Actions → Print Name Tags).
Tags are Print Formats on Function Check-In: Name Tag (used for browser printing) and Zebra Name Tag (ZPL, used for Zebra printers). To change the layout, duplicate the standard format, edit the copy, and select it in Check-In Settings.
Tick Print Security Codes in Check-In Settings for children's ministry: everyone checked in together gets the same random four-character code on their tag, and one extra Pickup tag listing their names and the code prints for the adult who collects them. The code is stored on each Function Check-In.
Name tags print the person's Nickname when they have one, and their first name when they do not. The pickup tag lists the same names.
Tick Print Allergies on Name Tags in Check-In Settings to print a person's allergies under their name, taken from the 'Allergies' field on the Person. Tags for people with no allergies are unchanged, and pickup tags never show allergies.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fci-h3-printers", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "🖨️Label Printer Setup", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fci-printers-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Choose how tags reach the printer under Name Tag Printing in Check-In Settings, set the label size (4 × 2 in is the common Zebra name tag, 2.25 × 1.25 in the common Dymo one), then use Print Test Tag:
- Browser: works with any printer that has a driver installed (Zebra, Dymo, Brother, an office printer). The browser's print dialog opens for each batch; pick the label printer and the label paper size once and the browser remembers it. To skip the dialog on a dedicated check-in computer, start Chrome with the --kiosk-printing flag and set the label printer as the computer's default printer.
- Zebra Browser Print: silent printing to a Zebra printer (e.g. ZD421) connected by USB or network to the station computer. Install Zebra's free Browser Print app on that computer, set the printer as its default, and accept this site when the app asks. Set Printer DPI to match the printer (203 or 300).
- QZ Tray: silent printing to any printer the station computer can see, sending ZPL. Install the free QZ Tray app and, if the label printer is not the default, enter its name under Printer Name. QZ Tray asks once to allow this site.
- Network Printer: no software on the station computer at all. Enter the IP address of a Zebra printer that is on the same network as the Churchit server (port 9100). The server sends the labels straight to the printer, so this needs a self-hosted server on the church network.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fciPrinterChurch1", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "More than one church. Each campus usually has its own label printer, so add a row under Printers Per Church in Check-In Settings for any church that prints somewhere else. Fill in only what differs: anything left blank in the row uses the settings above it. A station always prints to its operator's own church's printer.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "KbmdGnFK8k", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Bulk Check-In from the Person list
1. Open the Person list view.
2. Select (Check) the people you would like to check-in.
3. Click `Actions -> Check In`
4. Choose which Function for which you would like to check the people in.
The people's attendance will be tracked in the Function document.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "bLMhfdXsV3", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "🎵Songs", "col": 12}}, {"id": "7ts41_VmsH", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Songs can be added as items to a church function.
Note: there is not currently a way to present a song. This is planned in future versions.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ljVNwCikn3", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When creating a song, note the following:
- If you know the CCLI number for the song, add it. The Song Usage report lists it.
- You can add any number of slides to a song.
- After creating a song, you may want to add it to a function's schedule.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "song-usage-01", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Song Usage report counts how many times each song is on the Schedule of a function in a date range, with its CCLI number and the date it was last used. Use it to report song use to CCLI. It opens on the last six months.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "cc_h", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "🗂️Counseling Cases", "col": 12}}, {"id": "cc_b", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Counseling Cases are confidential case files (restricted to the Church Manager and Church Pastoral Care roles).
- Record the person, counselor, summary, and status.
- Each meeting is logged as a row in the 'Sessions' table.
- New Case Types can be added as needed.
- On a site with branch churches, only the person's own church can open a Counseling Case for them.", "col": 12}}]
